tooltips.revenueExplain: Revenue is the total income a company earns from selling its products or services. It is the most fundamental indicator for assessing a company's external growth. A company with steadily increasing revenue may be expanding its market share.
tooltips.opProfitExplain: Operating profit is the amount remaining after subtracting cost of goods sold and selling/administrative expenses (labor, marketing, etc.) from revenue. It is the most important profitability indicator showing how much money a company actually earns from its core business.
tooltips.opMarginExplain: Operating margin is the ratio (%) of operating profit to revenue. Even with the same revenue, a company with a higher operating margin earns money more efficiently.
tooltips.epsExplain: EPS (Earnings Per Share) is a company's net income divided by the number of shares outstanding. It represents 'how much each share I own has earned.' Rising EPS generally suggests higher potential for stock price appreciation. However, note that EPS can fluctuate significantly due to new share issuances or stock splits, so always check for changes in share count when interpreting EPS trends.
tooltips.yoyExplain: YoY (Year on Year) is the rate of change compared to the same period last year. By comparing with the same quarter of the previous year, it shows how much the company has grown, essential for understanding the company's true growth trend while excluding seasonal factors.
